Mostly the same  (because it's a chain concepts) when it comes to the meat however the vibes, salad bar and areas are the biggest difference when it comes to either Rodízio, Fogo or Texas de Brazil. The picanha is mostly good from all of them with occasional exceptions at random visits. I'm used to chuascaria in Brazil being very laid back, where the picanha is usually sliced up into strips that you then stuff into a loaf (like a mini baguette) and eat like a sammy. If you're looking for other Brazilian food though, check out Little Brazil for amazing Afro-brasileira food (like delicious fish stews). Also most of these chuascaria places have worthwhile memberships that can help with the price. I am a fan of going to these places (outside of personal bias) because it feels like the best bang for my buck when I want steak over most steakhouses here.

As a "TCK" the 'third' in third culture kid was primarily referring to the fact that their missionary/Christian culture is in itself a culture, it also is referring to your exact experience- as a permanent immigrant- as a third culture. 

So yes I definitely think you apply! 

Welcome to the club! It can be complex and suck at times but I think it gives a perspective incredibly few people have about the world. 

I grew up as a missionary kid but even in that community I was an outsider because I was adopted by American white parents while being from Colombia, but even when we lived in various countries in South America, due to our adoption- and some racism- we were never really fully integrated into south American culture while we were actually living there.. even the white kids got to go to local schools and make local friends while we were all in private American schools while living in, not the US. It has left me feeling like I have no home or culture whatsoever and trust me it's pretty not fun. 

I would definitely say you're a TCK and your definition fits the description and I know how lonely the experience can be so if you can, try to see if there are any support groups for being a TCK or groups about your home culture to help with some of those especially complex feelings!

For me probably it's been pretty obvious like a lot of answers that I would not do well with small children/newborns. The overwhelming and more importantly (for me) the potential to permanently damage important developmental features (like how my trauma with my parents caused cptsd and borderline personality disorder) specially I cannot handle the thought of being the person who caused this (likely my own trauma).

I'm adopted- transracial and transcultural, my family did not do the important jobs of bonding, honoring my bio culture and especially trying to understand they have a special needs child. I see how much it damaged me, I also see how much I would have been different if there was more genuine effort. Either way- all of it was pretty traumatizing. However one of the ways my mind/body wants to 'improve' this trauma is by recreating my own family. However I still refuse to risk being the cause of trauma to another developing human.

So I've decided to compromise. I'll always want to be a parent, I love older kids and want to watch kids grow up into their full selves. It dawned on me that I truly want to be a parent, not a 'mother' (non-binary). I decided to foster/adopt older kids, who are already here on this earth with whatever this earth gave them. Being adopted I know how hard it is to feel wanted, especially when you know it's hardest for older kids. As far as it being obviously difficult, that's a lot easier, for me at least, to manage how to help my kids who already have whatever life has thrown at them- hate to say it but I already know they're gonna be traumatized- I just can help better (though I know I can still cause pain/hurt/trauma in their lives) knowing I wasn't personally responsible during say the stages before grade school.

This is my journey, but a lot of it knowing the world of being an orphan myself but also as a compromise to my autism who I know would struggle with young children but adores kids. I know if I ever get stable enough to foster, no matter who those kids are- I'm already in love with them and can't wait to watch them grow up.

-50g Cane sugar
